title: Forward-mode automatic differentiation
outcome: Differentiate supported numerical functions and validate derivatives while preserving the numeric representation carried by dual numbers.

exercises.title: Differentiate analytically
exercises.task: Compute the gradient of x1 squared plus 3x2 squared at[2,3].
exercises.answer: An analytic case provides an independent reference for the AD implementation.

exercises.title: Check Jacobian axes
exercises.expected: Rows correspond to outputs and columns to inputs.
exercises.answer: A transposed derivative array can have plausible values but the wrong meaning.

exercises.title: Preserve numeric types
exercises.task: Replace a hardcoded Float64 buffer with similar(x).
exercises.expected: The dual-number path can retain derivative information.
exercises.hint: Use the input representation when the contract is generic.
exercises.answer: Ordinary evaluation alone does not reveal a differentiation-incompatible conversion.

exercises.title: Compare reductions
exercises.task: Differentiate a sum and a mean of two inputs.
exercises.hint: The denominator is part of the objective.
exercises.answer: A reduction change alters gradient scale and cannot be treated as a cosmetic refactor.

exercises.title: Inspect a branch boundary
exercises.task: Evaluate a nonsmooth function near its kink.
exercises.expected: A library result needs a differentiability interpretation.
exercises.hint: The executed branch is not a symbolic proof.
exercises.answer: At a nondifferentiable point, a returned convention should not be promoted to a unique mathematical derivative.

exercises.title: Validate a new gradient
exercises.task: Compare analytic or finite-difference directional behavior at several valid inputs.
exercises.expected: Use meaningful tolerances and retain failures.
exercises.hint: Separate approximation error from a wrong formula.
exercises.answer: Derivative checks should inspect shapes, scales and domain assumptions before optimization.
